items.title: Haywood Hillyer Interview, 1958-05-04
items.q: it takes somebody like, uh, uh, Edmond Sushant, or John, uh, Curran, John Curran, uh, what's her name, they're the ones that brought the jazz back, and got everybody interested in it, and stuff like that, and they all, but I wasn't present for that kind of stuff.

ctx.x: Well, can you tell me how long it lasted, when people stopped listening to it, and then when they started again?

Well, I think that there were a lot of these sweet bands that got popular. I mean, was Puron playing when you made your debut? But he died not too long after that. And then this, let's say, five or six years, or maybe a little bit longer than that, the people started going in for the, you know, the sweet type of music. Or during the 30s, they liked that type. And I think Puron, I mean, Salistan got his start back here at the pass. Because, you know, John Curran got him to come over here. And because all of our…
How old were you when you were at this party?
